sentences.text:
1. Heard SriRavi Sahu, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Rishi Kumar Prajapati, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and Sri Mohd. Shoeb Khan, learned A.G.A. for the State.
2.

The present application has been filed to quash the charge-sheet dated 18.06.2015 including cognizance order dated 22.07.2015 as well as entire criminal proceedings in Criminal Case No. 4258 of 2015 u/s 498A, 323, 506 I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station- Mahila Thana, District- Ghaziabad, pending in the court of A.C.J.M., Court No. 8, Ghaziabad.
3. Contention of learned counsel for the applicants is that dispute between the parties is matrimonial in nature.
Now, they have settled their dispute amicably and a compromise has also been entered into between them.

4. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has raised a preliminary objection that aforesaid compromise is yet to Pritam And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125413081/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 be verified by the court below, therefore, applicants may be directed to file aforesaid compromise before the court below for verification.
5. Considering the aforesaid submission, present application is disposed of with a direction to the applicants to file original deed of compromise before the court below, within a period of 15 days.

In case, such compromise is filed before the court below, the court below will verify the same after summoning the parties within a period of two months from the date of receiving the copy of compromise.
6. After verification of the compromise, court below will dispose of the impugned proceeding, in accordance with law.
7. It is further provided that for a period of two and a half months or till the verification of compromise, whichever is earlier, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants.
8. It is further provided that applicants are at liberty to file fresh application u/s 528 B.N.S.S., if required, to quash the impugned proceeding on the basis of verified compromise.
